_comment: SSoT for WHICH MODEL implements a role, with launch parameters and fallback order.
It is NOT the SSoT for which role/tier a do-feature step needs — that stays in
do-feature/SKILL.md (Model Routing Matrix), which by its own wording routes by TIERS,
not model names. Matrix answers 'this step needs tier X'; this file answers
'tier/role X is served by these models, in this order, with these parameters'.
Consumed by claude-home/scripts/model-run.sh. Edit here, never in a skill.

planner.purpose: Design, research, architecture, contracts, review. Quality outranks cost.
planner.order_rationale: External pools first, Anthropic last (user decision 2026-09-22, reversing the initial draft). Saving the scarce Anthropic quota outranks the latency cost here: gpt-sol at xhigh took 22.9 s vs 7.6 s for opus, which is the accepted 'small damage to speed'. RISK ACCEPTED: planning is the most expensive work to get wrong and the quality axis was never measured (Phase C cancelled), so this order trades an unmeasured quality risk for a measured quota saving. Revisit once the journal shows how often plans from external pools needed rework.

executor.purpose: Codegen, mechanical edits, test writing from a finished spec, bulk reading.
executor.order_rationale: External pools first: this is where the Anthropic quota is saved. Anthropic is the last resort so a step never dies for lack of a worker.

batch.purpose: Queued background work nobody waits on: corpus annotation, sweeps, scoring.
batch.order_rationale: Free-then-cheap. qwen costs no quota at all but 80-190 s per call, which is acceptable only when no human and no loop is blocked. sonnet-low sits last as a safety net so a queued job never dies when all three cheaper channels are penalised or exhausted.

orchestrator.purpose: REFERENCE ONLY — not dispatched by model-run.sh. The orchestrator is the main session, chosen by a human via /model at session start; a session cannot re-pick its own model from inside itself.
orchestrator.order_rationale: Listed so the choice is informed, not automated. A whole session can run on an external pool — `claude-glm` (no /model switch needed, the wrapper remaps tiers) or the Codex CLI — which is why they are listed first: the cheapest orchestrator you are willing to accept should be the default choice at session start. Note a session on claude-glm loses the four claude.ai connectors (Docs, Gmail, Calendar, Drive); the seven local MCP servers keep working.

tiers._comment: Mapping used by do-feature's Model Routing Matrix. Anthropic-only: the Agent tool cannot dispatch other pools.

opus-xhigh.notes: Fastest measured position at every context size.

fable-medium.notes: Twice the per-token price of opus and slower at high effort; keep for work that explicitly needs it.

sonnet-low.quota: Anthropic Max 5x — scarce, separate weekly Sonnet cap
sonnet-low.notes: Refused a word-salad test fixture under the AUP classifier; generate fixtures as coherent prose.

haiku.notes: Smallest Anthropic window. Fails with 'Prompt is too long' above ~170k tokens of usable context.

glm-5.3-high.quota: Z.ai Coding Plan — ~80 requests / 5h on Lite, resets on Beijing time
glm-5.3-high.notes: claude-glm remaps tiers: --model fable reaches glm-5.3. Reasoning cannot be disabled; only low/high/max exist.

glm-4.7.quota: Z.ai Coding Plan — ~80 requests / 5h on Lite
glm-4.7.notes: claude-glm remaps --model sonnet to glm-4.7. Window is ~205k, not 1M.

gpt-sol-xhigh.quota: ChatGPT Plus — 10-100 Sol messages / 5h, shared with ChatGPT Work

gpt-terra-high.notes: Best balance measured in the Codex pool.

gpt-luna-low.notes: Fastest non-Anthropic position at small and medium context.

qwen38.notes: Smallest window of any channel and 10-24x slower than every subscription pool. Batch work only. The only channel where code never leaves own infrastructure.

_policy_comment: unavailable = quota exhausted, gateway 5xx, auth failure, network down: the model is
genuinely unusable for a while, so a 1h circuit breaker avoids pointless retries.
context_overflow is not a fault — the model is fine, the task does not fit; jump to a
model with a bigger window instead of punishing this one.
timeout is NOT penalised by default: qwen legitimately takes 190 s, and penalising
slowness would evict the free pool permanently. Set penalize_on_timeout per model to

state_files._comment: Runtime state, machine-local. NEVER committed: it is state, not configuration.
